candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Convert mixed numbers or integers (and, when needed, pre-simplify a given fraction) into an equivalent fraction form suitable for subtraction.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S01 and B:S01 focus on converting mixed/whole numbers to improper/equivalent fractions; C:S01 covers the same conversions and additionally includes pre-simplifying a given fraction representation as part of form conversion.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator (often via LCM) and rewrite fractions as equivalent fractions with that shared denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts define this as selecting a common denominator (typically LCM) and scaling numerators/denominators to create equivalent fractions over that denominator.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are aligned (same denominator or separated whole and fractional parts).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the actual subtraction step after alignment, either subtracting numerators over a common denominator or subtracting whole and fractional parts.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express the computed difference in simplest accepted form by reducing fractions and/or rewriting an improper fraction as a mixed number or integer when appropriate.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts include reducing to lowest terms and converting improper results to mixed numbers/integers as the final formatting/simplification step.

alignment_summary: All skills align cleanly into four shared concepts with full 3/3 consensus. The only notable scope difference is Expert C’s conversion skill, which explicitly includes pre-simplifying a given fraction representation as part of converting number forms; this was aligned with the mixed/integer-to-fraction conversion concept.
